summary: Round 2 after verification: the compile-per-call finding survived, the ordering claim did not, and two advisory findings stand unvoted.

findings.description: The pattern table is compiled on every captured line, so a long build pays the compile cost once per line of output.
findings.recommendation: Compile the table once when the config loads and hand the compiled form to the capture path.

findings.description: Claimed that redaction runs before the line is split, so a token spanning a chunk boundary escapes.
findings.recommendation: None: the verifiers read the capture loop and found the split happens first.

verdicts.evidence: execx.go:212 splits on '\n' before calling redact.Line; the residue is carried in the scanner buffer.
verdicts.reasoning: A token spanning a chunk boundary is therefore redacted on the line it completes, so the claimed escape cannot happen.

findings.description: A finding's description is interpolated with `template.HTML`, so a review that says <script>alert('xss')</script> executes in the reviewer's browser instead of being read.
findings.recommendation: Interpolate as a plain string and let html/template escape it; there is no context here that needs raw HTML.

findings.description: No test covers the case where the pattern table is empty, which is the shipped default.
